name: @vymalo/vpay
//pnpm: JSON has no comments, so the justification for every entry under `pnpm`
lives here. `just audit-web` (pnpm audit --audit-level=high over the whole
workspace, dev dependencies included) is the gate these keep green; every
line below is a case where bumping the direct dependency could NOT clear
the advisory on its own. Dated, because an override that outlives its
advisory is a pin nobody meant to keep — re-check each on the next pass.
overrides['next>postcss'] — 2026-09-03. Four advisories against postcss:
GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q (high, CVE-2026-45623), GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (high,
CVE-2026-73646), GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 (moderate, CVE-2026-41305) and
GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp (moderate, CVE-2026-69153); all fixed in >=8.5.23.
Next pins `postcss: 8.4.31` EXACTLY, and still does on 15.5.25 (the
latest 15.x) and on 16.x — no release of Next unpins it, so there is no
version bump that clears these. 8.4.31 -> 8.5.x is a minor within the
same major, and it is the version `frontends/apps/dashboard` and
`frontends/packages/ui` already resolve for their own `postcss ^8.4.49`
devDependency, so the override dedupes the tree rather than splitting it.
Remove when Next's own pin reaches >=8.5.23.
overrides['@storybook/addon-actions>uuid'] — 2026-09-03. GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq
(moderate, CVE-2026-41907), fixed in uuid >=11.1.1. Storybook 8.6.14
depends on `uuid ^9.0.0`; the bump landed in Storybook 9, which is a
major migration of `frontends/packages/ui` (addon-essentials is dissolved
in 9.x) and out of scope for a dependency-audit pass. Scoped to the one
dependent on purpose: nothing else in the workspace resolves uuid after
the Cypress 15 bump, and a bare `uuid` override would silently apply to
whatever pulls it in next. addon-actions' only use of it is `v4()` for
action ids, which uuid 11 exports unchanged. Remove on the Storybook 9
migration.
overrides.vite — 2026-09-03. A COMPATIBILITY pin, and stated that way on
purpose: unlike the two above, it is not the thing that clears an
advisory, because vite 7.3.6 (what pnpm picks without it) is patched
too. What it prevents is a broken build. Nothing here depends on vite
directly — it arrives through `vitest` and through Storybook's vite
builder — and those two disagree about the range: vitest 3.2.7 accepts
`^5 || ^6 || ^7`, `@storybook/{builder,react}-vite@8.6.18` accept
`^4 || ^5 || ^6`. pnpm hoists one copy, so without this line it chose
7.3.6 and left Storybook on an unmet peer — measured, not assumed:
`pnpm --filter @vpay/ui build-storybook` is a step of CI's `web` job.
6.4.3 is the only version in the intersection that is ALSO patched for
GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff (high, CVE-2026-53571), GHSA-v6wh-96g9-6wx3
(moderate, CVE-2026-53632) and GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9 (moderate,
CVE-2026-39365), all fixed in >=6.4.3 — and it carries esbuild 0.25.12,
clearing GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99 (>=0.25.0). It is therefore a ceiling as
much as a floor, and the ceiling is the risk: should a vite 6.4.x
advisory land with the fix only in 7.x, this line has to go and the
Storybook 9 migration becomes urgent. Re-check on that migration.
